explanation: I found no Mathlib match, and I did not need a broad search to see why. The theorem is an unfolding step for the library's own `searchMap` (its version of minimisation, μ-search, on neighborhood-system domains). It is stated entirely with the library's own definitions: `ApproximableMap`, `toElementMap`, `vecElem`, `LamDef`, `searchMap`, and `natElem`, `zeroMap`, `succMap` and `cond` from its Example43 and Exercise326 files. Mathlib has no formalisation of neighborhood systems or approximable maps, so it cannot state this result. The proof only rewrites with the library's own lemmas (`searchMap_rec`, `head_push`, `tail_push`, `lamDef_coe_val`, `zeroMap_natElem_succ`, `cond_false`, `succMap_natElem`); the only outside step is an `omega` call to write `f (k ::ᵥ v)` as `m + 1`. All of the mathematical content sits in the library's definitions.
